manifest.title: A+ remains unproven—three probability-model challengers are rejected
manifest.description: Technical decision report on PolyMomentum strategy evidence, fresh-block power, and the path to A+.

blocks.body: # A+ remains unproven—three probability-model challengers are rejected

## Technical Summary

- **PolyMomentum remains A- and paper-only.** The strict-42 baseline earns `+$13.54`, but profit factor is only `1.114`, the second half loses `-$4.34`, Wilson is `0.684`, breadth is `19` profitable reports, and the five-report loss burst is `4`. The lifecycle alternatives remain rejected and unprofitable.
- **The measured strategy failure is overconfidence, but three distinct probability-model challengers now fail fixed evidence gates.** Fast volatility improved public-proxy log loss by `0.001040` but missed its Brier floor. DVOL covered only `33.33%` of registered forecasts under the frozen two-hour freshness rule versus `99%` required and was rejected before labels. The causal empirical-return CDF cleared aggregate Brier by `+0.000521`, yet improved log loss by only `+0.000302`, moved `93.84%` of forecasts farther from 0.5, and failed uncertainty, chronology, offset, and overconfidence-tail gates. All three families are rejected without retuning.
- **Binary-complement coherence has a negative structural prior.** In the registered interval, paired validity blocked `0 / 2,880` otherwise-valid orientations and caused no observable wait or ask erosion; residual magnitude, opposite pressure, and matched depth also added no observed selectivity. Actual candidate outcomes remain sealed.
- **Official settlement anchoring is mechanically correct but not yet supported by outcomes.** The label-free screen changed `215 / 2,778` fee-aware edge classifications across `21 / 24` markets. In the only retained signal-gated historical diagnostic, however, just `3 / 24` conditions produced opportunities: baseline selected one winner worth `+0.314523` in decision-time one-share payoff, while the official anchor filtered it and selected nothing, a paired delta of `-0.314523`. This is directionally negative and far too sparse for rejection, promotion, profitability, or A+ credit.
- **The active canary remains sealed at `310 / 750` with zero strategy scores disclosed.** Session 018 contributed 20 admissible conditions. Session 019 was interrupted by the VPS outage and remains fail-closed and unscored; bounded measurement-v5 session 020 is collecting after the service restart. The settlement-anchor candidate is frozen only for two later, disjoint `750`-condition blocks if it is pursued; it is forbidden from using the active block. No production runtime, paper, or live strategy change is authorized.

## Lifecycle changes reduced known losses but did not create a profitable strategy

Trailing v2 is the stronger lifecycle result, improving the tail baseline by `+$10.30`, but it still loses `-$2.29`, has profit factor `0.944`, payoff `0.157`, a four-loss burst, and a negative first half. Its apparent improvement is also concentrated in two folds. Immediate v1 is worse. These are mechanism rejections, not invitations to search neighboring thresholds.

## Entry confidence is the dominant economic defect

Across the 102 strict-42 trades, internal fair value exceeded the realized win rate by `8.03` percentage points. Market price was only `2.71` points below outcomes and improved Brier score by `3.87%` and log loss by `5.22%` relative to the internal estimate. Because simply copying the market removes the claimed edge, the strategy needs independent causal information that rejects unreliable edges. The paired-book gate fits that job: it uses contemporaneous complement consistency and no terminal labels.

## Fast volatility improves calibration too little to justify a strategy change

Before downloading or inspecting the registered public-window labels, the analysis froze a single mechanism: candidate volatility is the maximum of the existing `0.30` floor, rolling one-hour realized volatility, and the existing causal 15-minute-half-life EWMA volatility; baseline volatility is the maximum of the floor and rolling one-hour volatility. Across `8,633` complete five-minute BTC conditions and `25,899` forecasts at 120, 150, and 179 seconds, the candidate improved Brier score by `0.000177` and log loss by `0.001040`. Both chronological halves, all three offsets, the overconfidence tail, and both day-bootstrap lower bounds were positive. However, the preregistered overall Brier gate required at least `0.000500`; this was the only failed gate and it is decisive. The family is rejected without retuning. This public Binance direction screen establishes neither Polymarket opportunity selectivity nor executable PnL, and it authorizes no strategy, runtime, paper, live, profitability, or A+ change.

## DVOL cannot support the registered causal volatility test

The Deribit DVOL source contained `1,460` observations at exact six-hour cadence. Under the preregistered two-hour maximum age, only `10,080 / 30,240` fixed-offset forecasts—`33.33%`—could receive a fresh value, versus the frozen `99%` minimum. The source-feasibility gate therefore rejected `dvol_volatility_max_v1` before any Binance evaluation labels were downloaded. No staleness window, interpolation rule, date range, or threshold was widened after inspection, and no strategy, replay, runtime, paper/live, profitability, or A+ change is authorized.

## A causal empirical return law sharpens forecasts but fails robustness

The frozen candidate replaced the Gaussian residual law with a seven-day empirical distribution of exactly `2,016` strictly prior, fully terminal same-offset standardized returns. Across `10,062` non-tied five-minute conditions and `30,186` forecasts, aggregate Brier improvement was `+0.000521`, narrowly above the `+0.000500` floor, while log-loss improvement was only `+0.000302` versus `+0.001000` required. The candidate moved `93.84%` of forecasts farther from 0.5 and worsened the registered high-confidence tail. Both paired day-bootstrap lower bounds crossed zero; the first older subwindow lost on both scores; and 120-second log loss was slightly negative. Eight fixed checks failed, so `empirical_standardized_return_cdf_v1` is rejected without changing its lookback, smoothing, windows, offsets, or gates.

## The next decision remains the sealed canary

The probability-model branch has now tested a faster causal volatility scale, an external option-implied volatility source, and a non-Gaussian causal residual distribution without finding a gate-complete improvement. The exact table is retained instead of a new chart because the empirical decision is conjunctive across magnitude, chronology, offset, tail, and uncertainty checks; a visual aggregate would obscure the failures. Preserve the registered rejections and do not search neighboring parameters on these windows. Continue the active binary-complement block outcome-blind to `750` conditions, then build and hash-pin the separate measurement-only Linux scorer and evaluate the frozen rule once.

## The paired-book gate is structurally plausible but still only a hypothesis

Polymarket's Yes/No pair is fully backed by one dollar, while complementary orders can settle through transfer, mint, or merge paths and actual execution occurs at bid or ask. Coherence is therefore partly a market-mechanics constraint, not independent directional alpha. The mechanism only treats disagreement between both books' midpoints and depth-weighted microprices as uncertainty—not as free arbitrage or direct PnL. The fixed two-tick rule was frozen before forward scoring and is distinct from chosen-token pressure, calibration, delayed-entry, passive-entry, derivatives, and lifecycle families.

## Opposite-book pressure adds no observed feature information

A label-free reconstruction tested a proposed backup rule requiring `chosen pressure > 0` and `opposite pressure < 0`. Across `6,465` valid one-second paired states from all `24` markets, that paired predicate and chosen-positive pressure each fired `6,464` times and disagreed `0 / 12,930` orientation comparisons. Cross-touch mirror error was exactly zero and pressure correlation was `-0.999999`. The opposite-book clause is therefore rejected as a separate feature family in this observed population. This does **not** establish that chosen-token pressure predicts settlement or profitability. Coverage was `89.79%`, `735` states were invalid, native timestamps regressed `865` times, and the reference tapes contain internal gaps; the result is mechanism-screen evidence only and cannot change the sealed rule, grade, or promotion state.

## Residual magnitude has no observed selectivity after paired-top validity

The frozen two-tick residual rejected `0 / 6,465` valid one-second states in the 24-market BTC diagnostic and `0 / 1,403` valid states in its registered 120–180 second interval. All `735` unavailable full-window states failed the valid-top check; none failed for staleness or a missing snapshot. An independent public replication then captured five batches across 100 current non-candle binary markets: `490 / 500` paired states were valid, the registered Rust-equivalent threshold rejected zero, and even a fixed `0.002` threshold rejected zero. All seven nonzero cross-market microprice residuals coincided with depth mismatch and millisecond timestamp skew; midpoint residuals were always zero. This is label-free structural evidence, not settlement or PnL evidence. It means a future pass cannot be credited to residual magnitude without decision disagreements. A three-way post-block attribution—baseline eligibility, paired-book validity, and the frozen residual—was preregistered before opening any sealed outcome and is now implemented as descriptive-only schema-6 output. The current rule, thresholds, grade, and paper-only state remain unchanged.

## Paired validity caused no incremental wait in the retained candidate interval

The registered 120–180 second interval contained `1,403 / 1,440` valid pair states. Its `37` invalid seconds formed two episodes of `10` and `27` seconds in one market, but both outcome books were invalid throughout both episodes. Across the two possible orientations per second, the opposite-book requirement therefore blocked `0 / 2,880` otherwise-valid chosen sides. No pair-only recovery delay or executable-ask erosion was observable. This answers the structural wait-cost question negatively, but it is not a candidate or outcome result: signal, edge, state, labels, and the active forward block were intentionally absent. The sealed schema-6 score remains the only authority on actual decision disagreements and economic attribution.

## The fair-value anchor does not match the market's settlement source

The current model sends Binance RTDS current price and Binance window-open price into the binary fair-value formula even though these BTC five-minute markets resolve against Chainlink BTC/USD. A causal, label-free reconstruction held Binance momentum, Binance realized volatility with its `0.30` floor, the option formula, asks, fees, price band, and `0.07` minimum edge fixed; only fair spot and strike moved to Chainlink current/open. On `1,389` source-fresh paired states, the absolute fair-probability change was `2.02` percentage points at the median, `5.51` at p90, and `23.35` at maximum. That changed `215 / 2,778` orientation-level edge classifications: `112` proxy-only and `103` official-only, spanning `21 / 24` markets, `124` UP orientations, and `91` DOWN orientations. All `24 / 24` published prices to beat matched the captured Chainlink open to floating precision. This is distinct model-specification evidence, not trade or profit evidence: disagreements were concentrated `30 / 185` across chronological halves, terminal labels and strategy outcomes were excluded, and the active block is ineligible. An explicit offline-only evaluator now changes just fair spot/strike, enforces the frozen `10 s` current and `2 s` open bounds, rejects non-Chainlink inputs, pins the exact baseline hash, forbids grid/adaptive runs, and leaves the default harness and runtime unchanged. Its enforced allocation wrapper pins exactly 750 IDs, a fixed contiguous report partition with public strikes, the registered boundary's complete prior-block shape, every source hash, strict five-minute chronology, zero overlap, and three single-use report, trade, and paired-audit paths before replay data access. A separate label-free source audit verifies at least `95%` official-anchor coverage and the public prices to beat. The implemented paired scorer rehashes the PMXT, signal, settlement, fair-value, allocation, source-audit, report, and trade inputs; permits only the fair-value source to differ; and recomputes every registered economic, breadth, tail, latency, execution, and parity gate from raw fills. Synthetic pass, source-drift, path-reuse, and recomputed-failure tests prove the enforcement path without creating promotion evidence; all `545` Rust tests pass. No concrete future allocation lock can be issued until the controlling binary-complement condition set seals, so no anchor outcome, profitability, or A+ claim exists.

## The only signal-gated historical outcome check is negative and underpowered

A bounded retrospective replay of the same immutable 24-market July 15 capture exported `81` first opportunities after every non-edge strategy gate, representing only `3` independent conditions. All `81 / 81` official-source rows passed the frozen freshness limits. Under the existing Binance anchor, one condition barely cleared the fee-aware `0.07` edge floor at `0.072011`; it resolved as a winner and produced `+0.314523` of decision-time one-share payoff. Replacing only fair spot and strike with captured Chainlink values moved that edge to `0.001399`, selected zero conditions, and reduced paired payoff across all 24 captured markets by `0.314523`. This weakens the candidate's prior but does not reject it: the signal tape required official Binance one-second preroll and 44 bounded gap-fill seconds, the Chainlink tape could not satisfy the harness five-second settlement-continuity rule, repeated opportunity seconds are not independent, and decision-time one-share payoff omits latency, depth, fills, sizing, and state. The hash-pinned notebook reproduces the engine fair value exactly and revalidates every compressed and decompressed input. The forward contract remains frozen and unchanged; no retuning, runtime change, profitability claim, or promotion follows.

## Paired depth is mirrored, not a new uncertainty signal

A source-pinned, outcome-blind check reconstructed the nearest three levels of `490 / 500` current non-candle paired states. Every valid state passed a fixed `0.25` matched-depth ratio; the median ratio was exactly `1.0` and the minimum was `0.845`. A `$10` both-entry capacity reference rejected `20` states, but every failure came from the YES-side book: it added `0` rejections when YES was treated as chosen and `20` when NO was chosen. The four-side version rejected `30` states and was stable across the five snapshots, but that is generic liquidity selection already substantially represented by chosen-book depth and executable FOK checks. The paired-depth challenger is rejected as non-distinct and is not preregistered or implemented.

## A late-selection/payoff confound is visible without becoming a tuning lever

The registered screen may wait beyond the first baseline-eligible row until paired-book coherence appears, and that later row may reverse direction. This is causal, but a terminal classification win can occur near resolution at a top ask that leaves poor payoff after latency, depth, and fees. Before any forward score, schema 3 was frozen to publish selection delay, time to close, decision asks, final-minute selections, and direction changes. Those summaries remain descriptive only in schema 6: they cannot tune the rule, bypass the second block, or replace exact replay.

## Classification strength is no longer allowed to substitute for economics

The historical baseline's profit factor is only `1.114`. If winner and loss dollars followed the registered count minima exactly—`90%` winner retention and at most `70%` loss retention—the implied profit factor would be `1.433`. That leaves only `16.24%` deterioration in retained winner dollars before falling below the A+ `1.20` floor. Count retention cannot guarantee that dollar relationship. Schema 6 retains schema 5's normalized `$1` recorded-ask entry pricing, recorded entry fee, realized-support gates, unit profit-factor floor of `1.20`, and payoff floor of `0.20`; its new comparator attribution is descriptive only. This optimistic screen is necessary but not sufficient: latency, depth, fills, sizing, breadth, and tails still belong to exact replay.

## A 100-condition block would be statistically misleading

The baseline executed only `102` trades across `631` historical terminal conditions. At that nuisance rate, `100` conditions imply about `16.16` baseline candidates and `3.65` losses; the Wilson gate then requires an almost perfect selected record, and one loss moves the removal rate dramatically. At `750` conditions, the expected support is `121.24` baseline candidates, `27.34` losses, and `103.65` selected candidates at the registered effect. That is large enough for the existing gates to become decision-useful without changing the trading rule.

## Decision-useful support is now a hard gate, not an expectation

The blinded power amendment chose `750` conditions because that implied a `98.61%` chance of at least `100` baseline candidates, a `99.66%` chance of at least `15` baseline losses, and about `103.65` selected candidates at the registered effect. Schema 4 enforced only the 750-condition floor and ratio/economic gates, so an unusually sparse but nearly perfect sample could still pass. Before any forward strategy metric was inspected, schema 5 registered the realized minima explicitly: `100` baseline candidates, `15` baseline losses, and `80` selected candidates, matching the standing A+ minimum-trade policy where applicable. Schema 6 retains those gates exactly while adding non-gating attribution. The block is rejected at its fixed score if any support gate fails; collection cannot be extended adaptively. Measurement-v11 remains separately installed as the schema-5 predecessor with SHA-256 `07a386c7…4f00b89`, while the active v5 collector and production engine remain unchanged.

## Collection is progressing again, but still contains no strategy result

Eleven completed segments were terminal-only pending because the runner stopped checking Gamma after 60 seconds and the first refresh pass covered only the newest source root. A measurement-pipeline repair now uses a bounded 15-minute finalization wait and scans every registered source root. The repaired support audit reconciled 241 manifest rows to 241 unique IDs with no accounting or source failures. Subsequent bounded segments have lifted certified support to `310 / 750` without opening strategy metrics. Session 018 captured 24 conditions, admitted 20, excluded 4 under unchanged gates, sealed all five admissible groups, and deleted only its owned raw frames; its measured latency recommendation of `108 ms` does not lower the registered `202 ms` replay floor. Session 019 was interrupted by the VPS outage and remains fail-closed and unscored. After all PolyMomentum services restarted cleanly, bounded measurement-v5 session 020 resumed collection from the unchanged sealed support floor. No opportunity report, screen, candidate score, or promotion credit exists.

## Dynamic tick changes are real, but the frozen entry window remains causal

The current raw segment contained `24` tick-change rows across `6` markets, all changing from `0.01` to `0.001`; the earliest arrived `254.187` seconds after market open. Registered baseline-eligible rows end before `180` seconds, so the observed events do not overlap the strategy window. Gamma supplied no usable minimum tick for these markets, however, so a static `0.01` fallback was not safe for future segments. Before any score, the harness was amended to persist `0.001` only after a replayed top-of-book threshold crossing that occurred before the decision. A direct raw-to-v1 spot check found the preserved extreme book update `3 ms` after its explicit tick event. Measurement v5 now makes that check exhaustive and fail closed during conversion: raw frames cannot pass deletion preflight if a selected transition is malformed, differs from `0.01` to `0.001`, or lacks a reconstructable preserved book event. Completed v4 session 011 was not interrupted; active collection resumed as session 013 under v5 with zero restarts. The shared v1 format, fixed equation, two-tick multiplier, classification gates, and economic gates remain unchanged.

## A coherent score must now reproduce from the two recorded books

The schema-4 scorer previously trusted stored complement residuals without redoing the book arithmetic. That was an evidence defect: a token-wiring, serialization, microprice, or ask-alignment error could look like a successful uncertainty filter. Before any forward score, the scorer was hardened to require two distinct and stable token IDs, validate both raw books, recompute both microprices and residuals, align each best ask with the executable up/down ask used for unit economics, and reject extreme prices without the causal `0.001` tick. Four tamper tests now fail closed, while the full suite passes `501` tests. Scorer v6 is installed separately on the VPS; the active v5 recorder was not interrupted because its capture format already contains every required raw field. The rule, multiplier, schema, gates, and sealed sample remain unchanged.

## Exact replay now uses the same causal tick as the signal

The paired-book feature path already persisted a condition's dynamic tick, but executable replay still sized taker entries, quoted makers, stored positions, and rounded sells with metadata or a static `0.01` fallback. After a causal move to `0.001`, a visible `0.971` ask could therefore become a `0.98` FOK ceiling, changing both share count and edge; a `0.029` sell could be rounded down to `0.02`. That defect is now closed in both the research harness and cached live-replay, including an exit transition that occurs after entry. Three regression tests cover persistent condition state plus entry and exit quote rounding, and the full suite passes `504` tests. Measurement-v7 is installed as a separate Linux binary with the unchanged v6 scorer hash; production and the active v5 capture were not replaced or restarted. The current fee formula and crypto rate match the venue contract. Applying the fee once at multi-level VWAP is conservative before rounding, but aggregate L2 cannot reproduce match-by-match five-decimal rounding; that remains an explicit exact-replay limitation. No forward metric, fixed rule, screen gate, or capture row changed.

## Future live orders now retain the venue's current tick end to end

The live market feed previously discarded Polymarket's official `tick_size_change` event, while the order path reread Gamma metadata or used `0.01`. A promoted runtime could therefore disagree with exact replay or submit an invalid price after a dynamic transition. The source now keeps the latest timestamped tick per token, does not let a tick-only event refresh book age, resolves one causal condition tick across both outcomes, and uses it for visible-depth sizing, maker preflight, FOK rounding, signing, and submission. Two red-first regressions cover stale-event rejection, freshness separation, latest-feed selection, and causal book fallback; the complete suite passes `506` tests. Measurement-v8 is installed separately with the unchanged scorer, replay, and strategy rule. The production binary was not replaced or restarted, and active measurement-v5 session 013 stayed on PID `240334` with zero restarts.

## Future V2 fills now retain fee and lifecycle semantics

The authenticated live path still trusted a legacy top-level `fee_rate_bps`, sent `{}` instead of the documented `PING`, applied aggregate taker economics to managed maker legs, and booked at nonterminal `MATCHED` before deduplicating later status updates. A future live taker fill could therefore carry zero fee, a maker partial could be overstated, or a later `FAILED` transition could be hidden. The source now parses current Gamma `feeSchedule.rate` and `orderPriceMinTickSize`, snapshots the effective maker/taker fee with each pending order, computes the official five-decimal fee from the terminal confirmed fill, reconciles maker-specific legs, sends literal `PING`, and trips the breaker when fee or fill inputs are invalid. Four focused regressions and the full `510`-test suite pass. Measurement-v9 was installed separately; production and the active v5 canary were not restarted.

## Restart-safe authenticated recovery closes the last known live reconciliation gap

A venue could previously accept an order before the HTTP response reached the process, leaving no durable order id after a crash; WebSocket trade ids and pending position economics were also memory-only. Measurement-v10 now computes and atomically journals the V2 EIP-712 order hash before submission, restores only validated nonterminal orders, blocks new live orders until authenticated recovery succeeds, and polls confirmed trades plus order status every five seconds. Ambiguous submissions retain exposure. A terminal order may prove that confirmed trade evidence is missing but cannot invent fill price or fees from `size_matched`; the breaker stops instead. The complete suite passes `517` tests, and the separately installed Linux binary matches SHA-256 `03073aef…e08585f`. This closes the recovery implementation blocker but does not change the A- grade or authorize live trading.

## The fixed-support path remains bounded and outcome-blind

Segment 003 used `2.64 GB` of raw frames over 10,860 seconds and retained `120.1 MB` for 12 admitted conditions. Converting only already-admitted condition IDs projects about `6.99 GiB` of selected replay data at the full 750-condition floor. The VPS had about `12 GiB` free during the active segment-011 raw capture, while the collector preserves a `5 GiB` reserve and refuses a new segment if projected raw capture would breach it. This is operational capacity evidence only; it does not improve or reveal strategy performance.

## Methodology and source authority

Exact fee-inclusive replays and per-trade reconciliations are authoritative for historical strategy behavior. Each preregistration controls its own forward rule, condition allocation, and gates. The power, realized-support, residual-attribution, descriptive-diagnostic, unit-economics, causal-tick, paired-book reproduction, exact-replay, live-tick, live-reconciliation, and REST-recovery amendments were registered before any binary-complement forward strategy metric or screen existed. VPS service state establishes collector health only. The schema-6 scorer retains the schema-5 gates, requires both paired books to satisfy the existing 30-second replay freshness contract, pins every opportunity and resolution input by SHA-256, reproduces pair features and executable asks from raw serialized fields, prices normalized entries with the recorded fee rate, rejects inadequate realized support, and serializes descriptive comparator attribution including fee-aware PnL, profit factor, and maximum drawdown before any block can pass. Measurement v5 records explicit-to-preserved tick-transition integrity during conversion; measurement-v11 remains the separately installed schema-5 predecessor. A new hash-pinned schema-6 Linux scorer is intentionally deferred until the fixed floor authorizes scoring. The collector counts only fully sealed segments with complete resolution manifests and never reads strategy outcomes. The portfolio notebook rechecks file hashes, gate arithmetic, exact binomial support probabilities, Wilson calculations, economic alignment, and storage capacity. Separate executed label-free notebooks reconstruct paired-book pressure, residual, wait-cost, depth, and settlement-source anchoring; each is authoritative only for its bounded structural screen. The settlement-anchor page manifest independently pins all 24 public market pages and confirms their published Chainlink prices to beat against the captured open. The offline evaluator amendment now pins a default-off harness path, Chainlink-only provenance and causal-coverage audit, exact 750-condition/report allocation, public strikes, streaming SHA-256 verification for PMXT and every raw source, and three reserved single-use outputs. Its paired scorer recomputes the registered gates and requires exact catalog, strategy, execution, raw-input, and non-fair-source parity without changing the live or paper strategy. The fast-volatility screen was separately preregistered before its 31 official Binance one-second archives were downloaded or their labels inspected. It uses every complete five-minute condition in the fixed June 11–July 10 population, three fixed decision offsets, the engine's exact normal-CDF approximation, two chronological halves, a fixed overconfidence tail, and 10,000 UTC-day bootstrap resamples. The executed notebook and independent raw-archive validator reproduce all source checksums, `2,678,400` one-second rows, probabilities, scores, confidence intervals, and the single failed gate; repository-owned evidence paths are canonicalized so CLI and notebook outputs are byte-identical.

## Caveats, assumptions, and robustness

The `102 / 631` firing rate uses executed trades as a conservative proxy for reconstructed screen eligibility; exposure and state gates can suppress executions, so the forward screen may contain more candidates. Historical rates may drift, which is why the `750`-condition count and realized-support minima are fixed rather than adapted after collection. A sparse block is rejected rather than extended. The measurement-v11 build overlapped the first minutes of session 018's core window; zero restarts and zero new recorder warnings do not prove measurement neutrality, so that segment receives support only if the existing source-continuity and admissibility audits pass. The pressure, residual, wait-cost, depth, and initial settlement-anchor results are label-free mechanism screens. The BTC capture has incomplete one-hour warm-up, `865` native CLOB timestamp regressions, and reference-tape gaps; one-hertz reconstruction can miss sub-second transitions. Settlement-anchor orientations are edge-classification possibilities, not strategy candidates or trades. Fourteen otherwise-valid seconds failed the frozen 10-second Chainlink freshness limit, the sample contains only 24 markets, and disagreements were concentrated `30 / 185` across chronological halves. The retrospective outcome diagnostic improves relevance but not support: only three conditions reached the non-edge strategy gate, the Binance signal tape required official one-second preroll plus 44 bounded gap-fill seconds, and the captured Chainlink tape failed the harness five-second settlement-continuity check. Its one-share payoff excludes latency, depth, fills, sizing, exposure feedback, and tail clustering. The candidate deliberately retains Binance momentum and volatility, so it tests settlement-source alignment rather than a fully Chainlink-derived forecasting process. The independent public replication covers only five batches over roughly nine seconds; `10 / 500` pairs lacked one book side, pair timestamp skew reached `2 ms`, and observed REST arrays contradicted the documented best-first sort direction, so best prices were derived by extrema. The fast-volatility population is a public Binance terminal-direction proxy, not the strategy's gated Polymarket opportunities or official Chainlink settlement source. Proper-score gains do not establish edge selectivity, fills, fees, breadth, tail stability, or PnL. Seven exactly flat terminal conditions were excluded, yielding `8,633 / 8,640` conditions; forecast completeness was `99.919%` because those terminal ties have no binary label. Fifteen forecasts became negligibly more confident despite higher volatility because of the Black–Scholes variance term; the maximum confidence increase was `0.0000467`, and a post-score integrity amendment records the wording correction without changing the formula, dates, gates, or rejection. None of these diagnostics can support promotion, execution parity, settlement prediction, or profitability. Schema 6 applies recorded-ask entry fees, the existing A+ profit-factor/payoff floors, explicit realized support, and descriptive comparator attribution, but it still does not model latency, depth traversal, fill failure, stateful sizing, entry-state feedback, chronological breadth, or tail clustering. Those dimensions remain mandatory after two disjoint forward passes.

## Recommended next steps

1. Keep production in paper-only mode and preserve all existing A+ gates.
2. Continue the active bounded measurement-v5 binary-complement canary from `310 / 750`; retain the `5 GiB` disk reserve and 96-segment hard cap.
3. Count support only from fully sealed segments with complete ready resolution groups and passing tick-integrity manifests. Do not inspect strategy candidates, outcomes, rates, or economics before the floor.
4. Reject `fast_volatility_max_v1` permanently on its registered June 11–July 10 windows. Do not retune its half-life, floor, combination rule, dates, offsets, or thresholds, and do not implement it in the runtime.
5. Treat the zero pair-only exposure and zero residual selectivity as a negative structural prior for binary-complement coherence. Do not add neighboring coherence or paired-depth challengers.
6. When the fixed floor authorizes scoring, build and hash-pin a separate schema-6 Linux measurement binary; do not replace the collector or production binary. Score the frozen binary-complement rule exactly once and apply every support and A+ gate without retuning.
7. Preserve the frozen settlement-source-anchor contract without retuning: only fair spot and strike move from Binance to causal Chainlink current/open; every other input, threshold, fee, and gate remains unchanged. Treat the `-0.314523` three-condition retrospective result as a negative, underpowered prior with zero gate credit. Never score the candidate on the active block. If binary-complement block 1 fails and the anchor is still pursued, begin anchor block 1 strictly after that condition set is sealed and published; if binary complement passes, reserve the next disjoint block for its replication before starting the anchor.
8. For each future anchor block, issue one passing allocation lock that pins the exact 750 condition IDs, fixed report partition, public strikes, complete boundary-specific prior-block history, source hashes, zero overlap, and unused report, trade, and pair-audit paths. Run the label-free source audit, then evaluate with `--fair-value-btc-csv`, `--pin-input-artifacts`, `--settlement-anchor-allocation-lock`, and `--settlement-anchor-source-audit`. After both reports exist, invoke the paired scorer exactly once; accept only its raw-fill recomputation of at least `95%` official-anchor coverage, at least `80` candidate trades, every absolute gate, and exact non-fair source and execution parity. Reject the family on any failed gate and do not search neighbors.
9. Only two anchor-block passes may authorize one default-off runtime implementation and exact replay at at least `202 ms`. Do not reuse the existing broad live Chainlink switch, which also changes momentum. Promotion still requires positive executable fee-inclusive PnL in both halves, profit factor `>= 1.20`, payoff `>= 0.30`, Wilson `>= 0.70`, breadth, loss-burst, tail, causal-source, fill, fee, state, recovery, and live/replay-parity gates.

## Further questions

- Does actual candidate timing create any binary-complement decision disagreements despite zero pair-only exposures in the retained label-free interval?
- Does official Chainlink anchoring keep material decision selectivity across two disjoint chronological blocks, or was the `30 / 185` half split transient?
- Was filtering the sole historical baseline winner a sparse-sample accident, or does the same negative direction recur in fresh signal-gated conditions?
- Do official-anchor disagreements remove losses without sacrificing payoff, breadth, or either half of fee-inclusive PnL?
- Can causal Chainlink coverage remain above `95%` while preserving the frozen 10-second current and 2-second open bounds?
- Will source admissibility remain high enough to reach the active 750-condition floor before the fixed 96-segment cap?
